A full weekend of rope education, play and performance hosted by Ropes in Space. Aiming to break down geographical barriers to rope education in Scotland by bringing exciting teachers from further afield whilst also platforming local and up and coming teachers.

Ropes in Space is a community led organisation running peer learning events and rope jams in Glasgow. 

## Schedule

* Friday 7pm - 10pm: Intros and icebreakers. A chance to get comfortable in the space and get to know the other attendees in an informal environment. We will also run a "Speed Roping" (Like speed dating!) session to help break the ice. 
* Saturday 10am - 6pm: Workshops
* Saturday 7pm - 11pm: Rope Jam and Performances
* Sunday 10am - 5pm: Workshops

We will be running two classes concurrently throughout the event so you are not guaranteed participation in all of your preferred classes. We will send out registration forms to all ticket holders in due course and our full class schedule will be arranged to try to accommodate as many people's first choices as we possibly can. 

## Class List

* Cad and Evitrii (aka Bast): Freeform Suspension*, Rope Dance.
* Quartz and PeachyRopes: Shame, Objectification and Humiliation, Rope for Gender Euphoria*
* Brig and Belial: Wrestling with Rope
* Ginger and Farah: Embodied Tying
* Lola: Predicaments and Pain
* Mindorra: Hangers and Uplines and Locks, Oh My! *
* Setonix: Tying Decorative Corsets

*These classes will have requirements for entry.

## Requirements For Attendance

While we don't want to gatekeep attendance to Anchor point we do not recommend our event for absolute beginners to rope. 

A few classes will have some clearly communicated skill requirements for safety reasons and the majority of classes will assume basic competence with rope handling, understanding of basic safety and the ability to tie a few beginner level frictions and columns.

For those intending to solely attend as a rope bottom, some experience in rope and competency in communicating both your needs in rope and also knowledge on basic risk awareness such as the difference between circulation and nerve issues, is expected in order to facilitate good learning experiences and ensure safety for all.

If you are not sure about if you meet any of the requirements to attend feel free to reach out via message or discuss it with us at one of our peer rope events. There is still plenty of time to build these skills and we will be focusing on these competencies in our 101 and 102 sessions at our fortnightly rope gatherings in the lead up to the event. 

If you do choose to join us as a beginner and find yourself out of your depth we ask that you are prepared to sit back and follow as much as you can rather than divert the teachers or other participants to assist you during the class. 

## Ticket Info and Financial Transparency

Tickets are issued individually as we reconise that not everyone wants to attend events in a fixed tying partnership. Confident self-tyers are welcome to attend solo although not all of our classes will be easily adaptable for solo tying. Tying partnerships (up to 3 people) for each class should be arranged prior to registration opening as we will need this information to allocate classes.

We want to make this event as financially transparent and accessible as possible so we have decided to share our number crunching and let you pick your price - with a standard price of £150 for the whole weekend of workshops, Friday speed roping and Saturday Rope Jam and Performances. We are also offering payment plans of either 3 or 4 equal payments to increase access for those on lower incomes. Our teachers have kindly agreed a profit share model with us and our organisers are all working on a voluntary basis to enable us to offer this flexibility to you. If none of our standard prices are accessible to you or you need smaller installments to pay full price please apply for a solidarity ticket here and we will get back to you with an offer toward the end of the ticket sales period. 

* If ticket sales average £125: our teachers get a basic wage and RiS could add to our library or buy one or two comfier mats for tying on.
* If ticket sales average £150: our teachers get standard rope educator fee and RiS could add to our library or upgrade the majority of our mats.
* If ticket sales average £175: we're able to offer solidarity tickets to more people, our teachers get a higher level rope educator wage and RiS could get a second suspension frame.

## Airborne Disease Mitigation and Illness Policy

We recognise COVID-19 and other increasingly occurring pathogens are an ongoing risk to all and are especially impactful to disabled, chronically ill, and immuno-compromised people’s right to participate in public life and recreation. We will be taking steps to risk mitgation on this front and we ask all attendees to read and agree to our policy which can be seen in full on our Fetlife page.

## Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy

Our full Code of Conduct is published on Fetlife. We expect all attendees to familiarise themselves with, and abide by, our Code of Conduct for the duration of the event. We ask that a Fetlife or other kinky social media handle be included with all ticket purchases to allow us to properly vet all attendees. Our full Safeguarding Policy is available to read on Fetlife. We reserve the right to reject and refund a ticket purchase at the discretion of the organisers.

## Refund Policy

Full refunds, less processing fees, will be available via your Ticket Tailor account until the 4th of July at 6pm, when ticket sales will close. Any further refunds will be at the discretion of organisers.
